title: Company-wide policies and processes — access, change, data, procurement, vendor management, travel, templates
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Centralized reference for company-wide policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) covering access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and internal templates. This page consolidates policy statements, approval thresholds, and step-by-step processes to ensure consistent, auditable operations across Redwood Inference.
body:
Overview:

This document provides a single source of truth for cross-functional policies that affect all Redwood teams. It is intended for team leads, managers, system owners, finance, and people-ops. The policies below are mandatory unless an explicit exception is granted by Security or Legal and recorded in the risk register.

Scope:
- Applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors with accounts or access to Redwood systems.
- Covers corporate services, cloud accounts, internal tooling, procurement, travel, and vendor relationships.

Ownership and escalation:
- Policy owner: People Ops (owner_team).
- Security owner for access and data classification: Security & Compliance team.
- Finance owner for procurement and expenses: Finance & Legal.
- Any policy exception must be requested via /confluence/security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions and approved by the respective owners.

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose:
To ensure least-privilege access, enforce consistent onboarding/offboarding, and provide an auditable approval trail for elevated permissions.

Policy:
- Access model: role-based with three recommended roles per service: Admin, Editor, Viewer.
- Default access for new hires: Viewer on company-wide dashboards, Editor on their team resources upon manager approval.
- Admin permissions require a documented business justification and approval from the team manager + Security reviewer.
- All privileged accounts (Admin, service accounts with write access to prod) must use SSO + MFA.

Process (requesting access):
1. Submit an access request using the internal Access Request template (link in Templates section).
2. Manager approves via the HR access workflow in the Console.
3. Security automatically checks whether privileged access triggers an access review; if so, Security adds a reviewer.
4. Access is granted for a maximum of 90 days for temporary elevated roles and must be renewed.

Periodic reviews and attestations:
- Quarterly access attestations for all teams. Team leads must review and re-certify memberships for Admin/Editor roles.
- Automated alerts will be generated 7 days before temporary access expiration.

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Break-glass requests must be submitted via the incident runbook and include a post-facto justification and retroactive review by Security and the owning team.
- Emergency tokens are audited and revoked within 24 hours of issuance.

2) Change Management
Purpose:
Maintain service stability and ensure changes to production services are reviewed, tested, and auditable.

Change categories and approval thresholds:
- Standard change: Pre-authorized, repeatable (e.g., routine config updates). Requires team lead approval and CI evidence.
- Minor change: Low risk, no customer impact. Requires owner + QA signoff.
- Major change: Potential customer impact or schema migrations. Requires design doc, runbook, SRE review, and change window scheduling.
- Emergency change: Applied to mitigate a live incident. Documented in incident postmortem.

Process (submit a change):
1. Create a Change Request (CR) in the Change Management board with the following fields: summary, owner, risk level, rollback plan, test plan, target window.
2. Attach release artifacts and CI/CD evidence.
3. For Major changes: schedule a review meeting (design review) with SRE and affected teams at least 72 hours before the window.
4. During the change window: SRE monitors metrics (latency, error rate), and a designated 'safety engineer' can halt the rollout.
5. Post-change: record outcome, update runbooks if behavior changed, and close the CR.

Change windows and blackout periods:
- Standard maintenance windows: Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC for platform upgrades.
- Blackout periods: end-of-quarter and high-traffic events; exceptions require executive approval.

3) Data Management (classification, retention, handling)
Purpose:
Protect customer and company data through clear classification, handling rules, and retention schedules.

Classification levels:
- PUBLIC: Information safe for public release. No special protection.
- INTERNAL: Operational details not intended for public sharing.
- CONFIDENTIAL: Customer data, internal product plans, or financials. Requires access controls and encryption at rest/in transit.
- RESTRICTED: Cryptographic keys, PII with legal restrictions, and highly sensitive customer data. Access requires explicit approval and just-in-time access where feasible.

Retention and deletion:
- Default retention: 2 years for INTERNAL, 7 years for CONFIDENTIAL financial records, and retention rules for RESTRICTED data set per legal/regulatory requirements.
- Data owners must define retention and deletion policies in the data catalog.

Handling rules and tooling:
- All CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED data must be stored in approved services with IAM controls and logged access.
- Use the Data Catalog to register datasets; include owner, classification, retention, and approved processors.
- Backups containing RESTRICTED data must be encrypted and stored in an access-restricted bucket.

Breach reporting:
- Any suspected data exposure must be reported to Security within 4 hours. Security will initiate the incident response and notify Legal for regulatory assessment.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Purpose:
Ensure spending is compliant, budgeted, and auditable while reducing procurement cycle time.

Approval thresholds and channels:
- < $5,000: Team purchase card or manager approval. Submit expense through the Expense Report template.
- $5,000–$50,000: Requires Procurement ticket + manager approval + finance review.
- > $50,000: Requires Procurement ticket, finance approval, and procurement committee review (includes Legal for contract terms).
- Capital commitments > $250,000 require VP-level sign-off and multi-quarter budget alignment.

Preferred vendors and SOWs:
- Use preferred vendors listed in the Vendor Registry. Non-preferred vendor purchases > $25,000 must include a vendor security questionnaire and SOC 2 evidence where applicable.

Expense reimbursement rules:
- Submit receipts within 30 days; late submissions require manager sign-off.
- Per diem and per-night caps: see Travel Policy section.
- Corporate cards: issued by Finance; misuse may result in card revocation.

Process (procurement request):
1. Open a Procurement ticket with budget code, vendor details, and justification.
2. Procurement validates vendor, routes for approvals, generates PO or contract.
3. Finance processes payment only after receiving a valid invoice and PO reference.

5) Vendor Management
Purpose:
Mitigate third-party risk and ensure vendor relationships meet security, privacy, and contractual requirements.

Onboarding requirements:
- Complete Vendor Intake Form and register the vendor in the Vendor Registry.
- Risk assessment: low/medium/high based on data access, criticality, and integration.
- For medium/high risk: Security questionnaire and evidence (SOC 2, ISO 27001) required before onboarding.

Contracts and SLAs:
- Contract templates and standard SLA language are maintained by Finance & Legal. Deviations must be reviewed by Legal.

Periodic review:
- Annual vendor reviews for medium/high-risk vendors including a security posture check and invoice/usage audit.

Offboarding:
- Revoke vendor access within 24 hours of contract termination and remove integrations per the decommission checklist.

6) Travel Policy
Purpose:
Support business travel while controlling costs and ensuring traveler safety.

Pre-approval and booking:
- All international travel requires manager pre-approval and must be booked through the company travel provider.
- Use economy or premium economy for flights under 6 hours; business class requires VP-level approval for flights > 6 hours.

Per diem and lodging caps:
- Lodging cap: $250/night standard; $400/night in high-cost cities with prior approval.
- Meals: $75/day domestic, $100/day international (receipts required).
- Ground transport: use approved car services; mileage reimbursed at the current IRS standard rate when using personal vehicle.

Safety and incident reporting:
- Traveler must register itineraries with Security for trips to regions with elevated risk. Security will provide local safety guidance.
- Any safety incident during travel must be reported to People Ops and Security within 24 hours.

Expense submission:
- Submit expenses within 30 days using the Expense Report template. Attach itemized receipts. Out-of-policy expenses require manager justification.

7) Internal Templates (quick links and usage)
Templates available (links in the central Templates folder):
- Access Request template (for role changes and new access)
- Change Request template (CR)
- Procurement Request / Purchase Order template
- Vendor Intake / Risk Assessment form
- Expense Report template (with prefilled cost centers)
- Travel Authorization template

How to use templates:
- Always attach the relevant template to your ticket or CR to ensure the approvers have consistent information.
- Custom fields on templates are mandatory where marked. Missing fields may delay approvals.

Audit and compliance
- All approvals and ticket activity are retained for 7 years for financial and legal review.
- Regular internal audits will be scheduled to ensure adherence to these policies; non-compliance will be managed by People Ops and Finance with remediation plans.

Exceptions and change process
- To request an exception, submit an Exception Request into the Risk & Exceptions tracker with justification, duration, compensating controls, and risk owner.
- Exception approvals are timeboxed and reviewed quarterly.

Related links and resources:
- Templates folder: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates (centralized template library)
- Vendor Registry: /confluence/finance-and-legal/vendor-registry
- Data Catalog & retention rules: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-catalog
- Change Management board: /confluence/eng-platform/change-management

Appendix: Quick reference tables

Approval thresholds (summary):
- < $5k: Manager approval or team card
- $5k–$50k: Procurement ticket + Finance review
- > $50k: Procurement + Finance + Procurement committee

Access tiers (summary):
- Viewer: read-only
- Editor: write access for day-to-day tasks
- Admin: configuration and user management (requires justification and Security review)

Retention summary:
- PUBLIC: no special retention (as needed)
- INTERNAL: default 2 years
- CONFIDENTIAL: 7 years for financial records; otherwise defined by owner
- RESTRICTED: per legal/regulatory requirements

Contact points:
- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood-inference.internal
- Security (access & data questions): security@redwood-inference.internal
- Procurement & Finance: procurement@redwood-inference.internal
